meta.triageRationale: Reuses an already-fully-built feature (vscode-plugin/src/connections/* + command insrc.openDataSources) with zero new backend/data model work. The change is mechanical and has one obvious approach (add a MenuItem row + a switch branch + a PanelHost method that delegates to the existing command), but it touches 3 files across what are effectively 2 concerns (the panels module's menu/host surface, and extension.ts's wiring of panelHost to the connections host), which is more than a single-file trivial guard/rename/constant.

summary.prose: Adds a fourth entry, "Manage Connections", to the insrc status-bar click menu, alongside Detailed Status / Repo Configuration / Model Tiers. Choosing it opens the extension's existing, already-shipped Connections panel — the same panel the Command Palette's "Manage Connections" command and the Repo Configuration settings link already open. No new panel, UI, or backend capability is introduced; this Story only adds one more doorway into what already exists.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Add a Manage Connections entry to the insrc status-bar menu

api.name: WebviewPanelHost.openConnections

returns.meaning: No return value; this is a fire-and-forget dispatch, matching openDetailedStatus/openRepoConfiguration/openModelTiers.

preconditions: The host has been constructed via createWebviewPanelHost (vscode-plugin/src/panels/webview-host.ts), the same lifecycle every other open* method assumes.
postconditions: If WebviewPanelHostDeps.onOpenConnections is wired, it is invoked inside a try/catch, matching the module's established 'a sink throw must not surface (never-throw)' precedent already used by onDetailAction (webview-host.ts:298-303), onRepoConfigWrite, onRepoRegisterProviders and onModelTiersWrite — NOT the open* methods, which take no deps-callback and so set no precedent for this call.
A synchronous throw from deps.onOpenConnections is caught and logged via deps.logger.warn; it never propagates out of openConnections() or showStatusMenu()'s dispatch.

If it is NOT wired, deps.logger.warn is called once and nothing else happens — there is no placeholder body to render for an externally-owned panel, unlike repoRenderer/modelTiersRenderer which fall back to an in-host placeholder.

api.name: WebviewPanelHost.showStatusMenu

returns.meaning: Resolves once the user's QuickPick choice has been routed to the matching open method, or settles immediately on dismiss (Esc).

preconditions: deps.pickMenu is wired (unconditional dependency, unchanged from today).
postconditions: MENU_ITEMS now carries 4 entries; a chosen.action === 'connections' routes to this.openConnections().
The existing three branches (detailed/repoConfig/modelTiers, vscode-plugin/src/panels/webview-host.ts:527-541) are unchanged in behavior and order.

dataModelChanges.details: The action union gains a 4th literal member 'connections', alongside the existing 'detailed' | 'repoConfig' | 'modelTiers'. No other field of MenuItem (label) changes.

New OPTIONAL onOpenConnections?: () => void field. Its INVOCATION in openConnections() follows the module's 'a sink throw must not surface (never-throw)' precedent (try/catch + logger.warn, matching onDetailAction/onRepoConfigWrite/onRepoRegisterProviders/onModelTiersWrite), not the open*-method fallback-to-placeholder style: there is no placeholder body for an externally-owned panel, so an unwired dep logs a warning and opens nothing.
The module-level MENU_ITEMS array gains a 4th row { label: 'Manage Connections', action: 'connections' }, appended after the existing Model Tiers row.

errorCases.scenario: The host is constructed without WebviewPanelHostDeps.onOpenConnections wired (e.g. an older extension.ts build, or a test fake that omits it) and the user picks 'Manage Connections' from the menu.
errorCases.detection: openConnections() checks deps.onOpenConnections via optional chaining (deps.onOpenConnections?.()); the call resolves to undefined when unwired.
errorCases.response: deps.logger.warn(...) is called once with a message naming the missing wiring; no panel opens and no exception is thrown.
errorCases.userImpact: The menu item is selectable but silently does nothing beyond the warning (visible only in the extension's own output channel, not a user-facing toast) — identical degrade style to how repoRenderer/modelTiersRenderer being unwired falls back to a placeholder instead of crashing.

errorCases.scenario: deps.onOpenConnections, when wired, throws synchronously (a host-level contract case, provable with a throwing test fake) — OR, separately, its real production binding (connectionManager.open(), an async method) returns a promise that rejects. host.ts:93-113 shows open()'s body has synchronous calls (createPanel(), panel.setHtml(...), panel.reveal(), this.#bindTest()) that run BEFORE its one internal try/catch; because open() is declared async, a throw from any of them is converted into a REJECTED promise, not a synchronous exception — so open() is not proven never to reject.
errorCases.detection: openConnections() wraps deps.onOpenConnections?.() in try/catch (matching the sink precedent) and catches a SYNCHRONOUS throw there. That try/catch cannot catch an asynchronous rejection from a promise the callback fires-and-forgets (JS try/catch does not catch rejections of an unawaited promise) — so the real production wiring additionally attaches its own .catch to connectionManager.open()'s returned promise in extension.ts, independent of openConnections()'s try/catch.
errorCases.response: A synchronous throw is caught by openConnections()'s try/catch and logged via deps.logger.warn, exactly like the other deps-callback sinks. A rejected connectionManager.open() promise is caught by extension.ts's own .catch on the wiring and logged there — neither path leaves an unhandled exception or an unhandled promise rejection.
errorCases.userImpact: No surfaced error in either case: the panel simply fails to open, with a warning logged (host-side logger.warn for a sync throw, or the extension.ts wiring's own warn for an async rejection).

edgeCases.input: The user opens the status-bar menu and picks 'Manage Connections' while the Connections panel is already open.
edgeCases.expected: connectionManager.open() is the SAME existing method the Command Palette command already calls today, so this Story inherits its existing create-or-reveal semantics unchanged — this Story adds no new logic to decide that behavior.

edgeCases.input: The user dismisses the QuickPick (Esc) without choosing any of the 4 items, including the new one.
edgeCases.expected: showStatusMenu() returns immediately (chosen === undefined check at vscode-plugin/src/panels/webview-host.ts, unchanged) — no open* method, including openConnections(), is called.

edgeCases.input: A test constructs createWebviewPanelHost with a fakes object that has every OTHER optional dep (repoRenderer, modelTiersRenderer, etc.) wired but omits onOpenConnections specifically.
edgeCases.expected: Only the Connections menu item degrades (warn + no-op); Detailed Status / Repo Configuration / Model Tiers continue to open normally — the four open* methods are independent, matching the existing pattern where modelTiersRenderer being unwired does not affect repoRenderer.

invariantsToPreserve.text: MenuItem.action is a closed union with no default/fallthrough case in showStatusMenu's dispatch (today: if/else-if/else over 'detailed'/'repoConfig'/'modelTiers', the final else implicitly catching 'modelTiers') — adding 'connections' must keep every branch an explicit check, not silently fall into an existing branch's final else.

Every optional WebviewPanelHostDeps field added after the S004 shell (repoRenderer, onRepoConfigWrite, onRepoRegisterProviders, modelTiersRenderer, onModelTiersWrite) degrades gracefully when unwired rather than throwing — onOpenConnections must follow the same contract.
The panels module (vscode-plugin/src/panels) imports nothing from connections/* today — this Story must not introduce that import (a1's design already avoids it).

Every existing optional deps-callback SINK in webview-host.ts (onDetailAction, onRepoConfigWrite, onRepoRegisterProviders, onModelTiersWrite) wraps its invocation in try/catch with the documented rule 'a sink throw must not surface (never-throw)' (webview-host.ts:298-303 et al.) — onOpenConnections must follow this SAME precedent, not the unguarded open*-method dispatch style this LLD originally (incorrectly) cited.

testLevels.purpose: Verify MENU_ITEMS/showStatusMenu dispatch and openConnections() in isolation over fakes, matching the existing webview-host.test.ts pattern used for the detailed/repoConfig/modelTiers entries.

migration.stateBefore: MENU_ITEMS (vscode-plugin/src/panels/webview-host.ts:52-56) carries 3 entries; MenuItem.action (vscode-plugin/src/panels/types.ts:224-228) is 'detailed' | 'repoConfig' | 'modelTiers'; showStatusMenu (webview-host.ts:527-541) dispatches via if/else-if/else over those 3; WebviewPanelHostDeps (types.ts:249-310) has no connections-related field; extension.ts wires the Connections panel independently via registerConnectionCommands (connections/wiring.ts:12-20) directly to connectionManager.open(), with no path through WebviewPanelHost.
migration.stateAfter: MENU_ITEMS carries 4 entries; MenuItem.action is 'detailed' | 'repoConfig' | 'modelTiers' | 'connections'; showStatusMenu dispatches to a new openConnections() on a 4th explicit branch; WebviewPanelHostDeps carries an optional onOpenConnections?: () => void field; extension.ts additionally wires onOpenConnections: () => void connectionManager.open() when constructing the panel host, alongside its existing registerConnectionCommands wiring (which is left untouched).

migrationSteps.action: Add the 'connections' literal to MenuItem.action's union (types.ts) and add onOpenConnections?: () => void to WebviewPanelHostDeps (types.ts), plus an openConnections(): void member on WebviewPanelHost (types.ts).

Add a 4th MENU_ITEMS row ({ label: 'Manage Connections', action: 'connections' }), an openConnections() implementation that invokes deps.onOpenConnections?.() inside a try/catch + logger.warn (matching the onDetailAction/onRepoConfigWrite/onRepoRegisterProviders/onModelTiersWrite sink precedent), and a 4th showStatusMenu dispatch branch to webview-host.ts. Also rename and extend the existing 'showStatusMenu offers EXACTLY three items...' test to the 4-item list.

In extension.ts, pass onOpenConnections: () => { connectionManager.open().catch((err) => logger.warn(...)); } into the panelHost construction — attaching its own .catch to the promise connectionManager.open() returns (defense-in-depth against a rejection; host.ts's open() is not proven never to reject, see errorPaths) — reusing the connectionManager instance already constructed for registerConnectionCommands.

migration.backwardCompat: Purely additive: a 4th union member and a new optional dependency field are both additive TypeScript changes with no removed/renamed members, so any existing caller or test fake that omits onOpenConnections keeps compiling and behaves exactly as it does today (openConnections() degrades to a warn, not a throw). No existing command id, panel, or IPC shape changes.

alternativesConsidered.name: Plain injected open callback
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a bare onOpenConnections?: () => void dependency; a new openConnections() method calls it.

alternativesConsidered.name: Typed Pick<ConnectionsManagerHost,'open'> dependency
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Inject the connections host's own open()-only slice, typed via Pick<ConnectionsManagerHost,'open'>, exactly mirroring registerConnectionCommands' own parameter type.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally equivalent to a1 but trades a clean module boundary for type precision the Story does not need — requires types.ts's first import from connections/host.ts, coupling two module families s1 found wired independently today.

alternativesConsidered.name: Generic command-execute passthrough
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Inject a generic executeCommand(id: string): void dependency; openConnections() calls it with the literal 'insrc.openDataSources' command id.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Introduces a stringly-typed, broader-than-needed capability and breaks the module's established narrow-callback idiom — no other WebviewPanelHostDeps field is a generic command-id executor.
